title: Quiescent SLA savings — mini benchmark
summary: Lightweight field notebook exploring cost vs latency for exploiting quiescent windows in sessionized workloads. Compares three runtime strategies (always-hot, opportunistic-slot, hybrid-stagger) with synthetic microconversation traces and a small 1M-token throughput projection.
objective: Decide whether to prototype a quiescent-aware slot policy for low-cost tiers that preserves p90 latency within 10% of baseline while reducing $/1M token by at least 12% on target mixes.
notes: This is a quick exploratory benchmark built from trace-sampled microconversation logs (internal sample set: MCV-2028-q4). Numbers intentionally lightweight — not production SLA claims. Focus is directional: where are the low-hanging savings without regressing mid-percentiles?
experiment-setup:
Workload: sessionized chat mix derived from MCV-2028-q4 (70% short-turn, 25% medium, 5% long). Baseline infra profile: x1 GPU pool equivalent (inferred cost unit). Synth driver simulates arrival cadence with real inter-message gaps. Three policies:

  - always-hot: keep a prewarmed slot allocated to a session until explicit teardown (current conservative default for premium tiers)
  - opportunistic-slot: slotize only while active message stream; idle > 200ms releases slot and relies on fast prewarm path on next request
  - hybrid-stagger: keep low-priority prewarm token (best-effort wake within 50ms) for sessions with <3s inactivity; longer gaps release completely

Each run simulated 100k sessions to stabilize p99 sampling. Cost estimate model: amortized GPU-hour cost + warmup energy penalty (warmup cost approximated as 0.02 GPU-hour per warm). Latency measures capture 50/90/99 percentiles for user-observed decode start (ms).
key-metrics-table:
ASCII table below: cost normalized to baseline (always-hot = 1.00). p50/p90/p99 in ms. $/1M tokens is projection using baseline token-rate and GPU-hour cost assumptions.

Policy           | cost_norm | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | p99(ms) | $/1M tokens
-----------------|-----------|---------|---------|---------|------------
always-hot       | 1.00      | 42      | 112     | 380     | 1200
opportunistic    | 0.81      | 48      | 128     | 520     | 980
hybrid-stagger   | 0.88      | 44      | 118     | 410     | 1060

Notes: opportunistic gives biggest dollar savings but increases p99 considerably. Hybrid captures most savings while keeping p99 within ~8% of baseline on median runs.
latency-cost-tradeoffs: Observed trade-offs: opportunistic-slot reduces steady-state amortized cost via higher slot turnover; however heavy-tailed warmup latencies appear at p99 due to bursty re-joins. Hybrid-stagger smooths those re-joins by retaining cheap soft-prewarm tokens for short idles, which reduces p99 spikes. For user-facing SLAs (p90-driven), opportunistic is acceptable if p99 bursts are handled by fallback routes or lower SLA tiers.
microchart-waveform:
Simple ascii waveform of session gaps and wake events (one sample session):

Times(ms)  : 0      200     500    1100   4200   4300
User events: msg1  -> idle -> msg2  -> idle ->  msg3 -> msg4
Policy reaction (opportunistic): release after 200ms -> warm on msg2 -> warm penalty observed
Policy reaction (hybrid): retain soft-prewarm until 3s -> msg2 no warm penalty -> release -> rewarm for msg3

Implication: short inter-message gaps (200ms-2s) are the win surface for hybrid policies.
regression-risk: Primary risk vectors: p99 regressions that correlate with user-visible burst patterns; billing/observability mismatch if warmup costs are not attributed correctly; complexity in runtime policy heuristics creating brittle corner cases for multiplexed tenants. Mitigations: staged rollout on low-tier customers, p99 shadowing, automatic fallback to always-hot if p99 breach detected.
operational-notes: Implementation sketch: lightweight soft-prewarm token (stateless marker) stored in fast cache keyed by session id; eviction window parameterized (default 3s). Scheduler: low-priority background prewarm with capped concurrency to avoid amplifying bursts. Telemetry: emit 'soft-prewarm-hit' and 'warm-restart' events; add p99 warm latency alert tied to session cohort. Cost accounting: record warm CPU/GPU-seconds per warm and attach to tenant usage to track real dollar impact.
conclusions:
1) Opportunistic-slot gives the largest cost reduction (~19%) but has unacceptable p99 spikes for default SLA profiles.
2) Hybrid-stagger is a practical middle ground: ~12% cost reduction with p99 within ~8% of baseline in our synthetic runs.
3) If product wants an aggressive low-cost offering (developer/experimental tier), opportunistic-slot could be acceptable with explicit lower SLAs and client-side retry guidance.

Recommendation: prototype hybrid-stagger in a canary region with 5% traffic and full p99 shadow monitoring; capture warmup accounting for billing experiments.
